title: SOLANA PRE-REGISTRATION ADDENDUM — SOL 2026-07-30 launch batch

disclosure.header:
scope: solana | applies to: prereg/solana/20260730_164140_solana_preregistered_at_prediction.json
             (commit 19429dd, batch_root 2021bf22…0712fafe, n=46)
issued: 2026-08-03T11:25:07Z | outcomes known at issue: NONE (14-day horizon resolves 2026-08-13)
disclosure.what_happened:
The 07-30 Solana manifest contains 46 predictions across the 23-pool founding cohort —
two complete frozen batches, not one:
  batch 1 — frozen 2026-07-30T12:31:18Z, span_days 14.0154, published 4h10m22s later
  batch 2 — frozen 2026-07-30T16:40:53Z, span_days 14.1887, published 47s later
Both cleared the protocol-14 lookback gate (unlock 12:09:08Z); neither is pre-unlock.
Batch 1 was produced by an operator invocation intended as a dry run. The run wrapper's
DRY_RUN flag suppresses publication but does not suppress the freeze, so real predictions
were written and held unpublished until the second run's emit swept them in.
disclosure.what_differs:
The two batches are distinct claims, not duplicates: prediction bounds, vol_input,
fee_rate_input, mc_seed and prediction_hash differ for all 23 pools; y_prob differs for 10.
Frozen bands are identical across both — no cohort or band drift. Divergence is small
(max Δy_prob 0.0032, avg 0.0005) and driven by per-run Monte-Carlo seed re-randomization
plus four hours of additional collector data.
disclosure.the_label_defect:
All 46 rows carry tier `preregistered_at_prediction`, which asserts publication at prediction
time. That is accurate for batch 2. For batch 1 the freeze→publish gap was 4h10m22s, so those
predictions existed privately before commitment; the tier label overstates their publication
latency. All timestamps were and remain in the published manifest — nothing is falsified.
The published record is not modified, deleted, or rewritten. This addendum corrects the label
by disclosure.
disclosure.canonical_batch_rule:
When multiple frozen batches exist for the same prediction window, the canonical set is
  the one whose freeze→publish latency satisfies the tier-3 claim.
Applied here: batch 2 (47s) is canonical and governs grading on 2026-08-13. Batch 1 is
retained in the public record as informational and is NOT graded.
Rationale: the batches are near-duplicates, so grading both would treat 46 correlated rows
as 46 independent observations — inflating apparent sample size and understating variance in
the calibration statistics. One set must govern. This rule is adopted while all outcomes are
unknown, so the selection cannot be outcome-motivated, and it applies to any future
recurrence without further judgment.
disclosure.remediation:
The run wrapper is being changed so a dry run cannot write the production prediction store,
and so a freeze is refused if a batch already exists for the current UTC day.
